searchText: I would prefer returning a new object. This would mean that these endpoints can return a heterogenous array in case the node has both types of attestations in the pool. inclined to agree This would probably necessitate a `v2` for Electra i.e. would prefer avoiding heterogeneous object list return well, lesser evils in order to avoid this, it should be explicitly mentioned in the spec that `v1` returns pre-Electra attestations and `v2` returns post-Electra ones yes probably otherwise clients' implementations may differ and realistically I'm not sure it makes sense to "mix" the attestations anyway in clients, though I guess in the upcoming interop there might be some discussion about deneb attestations in electra which traditionally has worked by default because the attestation format hadn't changed i.e. there was no real problem attesting to capella blocks in deneb, mechanically Yeah, this might realistically happen only at the beginning of Electra. The pool might have some Deneb atts sitting in it when the fork happens and that's edge-casey enough I'd want to see compelling evidence it has to be handled to add permanent complexity for a situation which will last maybe a couple epochs relevant to this API design because in general they won't be mixed anyway Agreed it's an edge case. Maybe it is enough to add a fork/version dropdown that changes the result schema and example And stay on `v1` well, as long as it doesn't break compatibility with existing `v1`, that seems potentially ok too opened this https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/445 just to dump it somewhere. I might have been inaccurate.
